No, the bank cannot foreclose. In a lien theory state, the majority view is that a mortgage is only a lien and doesn't transfer title, so one joint tenant's mortgage does not sever the joint tenancy. When the partner died, the woman took the whole property by survivorship, his interest and the bank's lien on it ended, and the bank has nothing to execute against. The team note says the opposite, but that describes the title theory approach, not the lien theory majority.

CONFIDENCE: 85
